Heard Sri Avinash Chandra Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Hridesh Bhartiya, learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri R.P. Patel, learned State Law Officer and perused the material placed on record.

2. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 1068 of 2023, U/S 363, 376 IPC and 5J(2)/6 POCSO Act,
Police Station Pipraich, District Gorakhpur, during the pendency of trial.

3. In compliance of the order of this Court dated 16.1.2025, the informant/complainant herein is in Court and she has stated that she mistakenly got the FIR registered and now, she has shown her Gulshan Kumar Nishad vs State Of U.P. 1 willingness that the applicant be released from jail.
4. As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to have enticed away the minor daughter of the informant aged about 17 years 10 months on 11.12.2023 at about 9.00 am.
5.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case with a view to cause unnecessary harassment and to victimize him.
It is stated that he has nothing to do with the said offence.
It is stated that FIR is delayed by more than one day and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
The said FIR has simply been lodged on the basis of suspicion only but subsequently, in the statement of the victim recorded u/s 164 Cr.P.C., the allegations of rape have been levelled.
6. It is stated that the victim is the consenting party, as is evident from the circumstances.
Learned counsel has informed that out of the said wedlock, a baby girl has been born and he is ready to take care of his wedded wife and the offspring.
7. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
8. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 20.10.2024.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
9. Learned State Law Officer and learned counsel for the informant vehemently opposed the bail application but have not disputed the aforesaid submissions of learned counsel for the applicant.

10. In light of the judgement of the Supreme Court passed in Niranjan Singh and another vs.
Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and others AIR 1980 SC 785 this Court has avoided detailed examination of the evidence and elaborate documentation of the merits of the case as no party should have the impression that his case has been prejudiced.

entities.text:

Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and others AIR 1980 SC 785
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A prima facie satisfaction of case is needed but it is not the same as an exhaustive exploration of the merits in the order itself.
11. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

12. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
13.

sentences.text: It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that ?bail is a rule and jail is an exception?.
14. Learned State Law Officer could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
15. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned State Law Officer.

16. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

17. Let the applicant- Gulshan Kumar Nishad involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall deposit an amount of Rs. 50,000/- in the account of the offspring of the couple as an F.D. within six months.
(ii) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(iii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C./351 B.N.S.S.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
18. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

19. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
